The '''2021–22 season''' was the [[List of FC Barcelona seasons|123rd season]] in the existence of '''[[FC Barcelona|Futbol Club Barcelona]]''' and its 91st consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. In addition to the [[2021–22 La Liga|domestic league]], Barcelona participated in this season's editions of the [[2021–22 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], the [[2021–22 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]], the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], and the [[2021–22 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]], entering the latter competition for the first time since [[2003–04 UEFA Cup|2003–04]]. This was also the first season since [[2003–04 FC Barcelona season|2003–04]] not to feature [[Lionel Messi]], who transferred to [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] after his contract expired.

The season was a tumultuous one, as Barcelona's economic problems forced the departure of [[ Lionel Messi|Messi]] and [[Antoine Griezmann|Griezmann]], in addition to not being able to replace them with quality players. Barcelona finished third in their Champions League group and failed to reach the knockout stages for the first time since 2003, when it competed in the UEFA Cup after a disastrous domestic campaign the [[2002–03 FC Barcelona season|previous season]]. Furthermore, poor domestic form saw Barça drop as low as ninth in the league by late October, which triggered head coach [[Ronald Koeman]]'s sacking. He was replaced by a club legend [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]], who managed to reverse the team's fortunes with new winter signings [[Ferran Torres]] and [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]]. The team's highlight of the season was the 4–0 thrashing of [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] at the Bernabéu, which helped propel them to the second place in the standings, one they never relinquished for the rest of the campaign. However, April saw Barcelona get knocked out of the Europa League by [[Eintracht Frankfurt]]. Coupled with several league stumbles in April and May, in addition to earlier defeats in the Supercopa de España and Copa del Rey, Barça ended up trophyless, never managing to catch up with runaway leaders Real Madrid.

===Kit information===
This was the final season of Rakuten as Barcelona's main sponsor shirt before replaced by [[Spotify]] next season.

*'''Home''': The home kit featured unusual design, instead of blue and red stripes, or halves, or any of the variations used in recent years, the new Barcelona home kit took the graphics from the club crest and applies to the entire front. The shorts were also very unusual, featuring half blue and half red sides together with two blue and red hoops socks. The home kit was used for La Liga and Copa del Rey matches.
*'''Home (European)''': Barcelona also released the home kit for European matches. The kit features traditional Barcelona stripes with illustrations that highlighted landmarks of various Barcelona neighborhoods inside the stripes (these include, among others, the three chimneys of Poble Sec or the original La Masia, which is located next to the Camp Nou). The blue shorts and navy socks completed the set.
*'''Away''': The away kit was purple with a shiny iridescent logo and with the blue and red stripes on the sides, purple shorts with blue and red stripes and purple socks completing the set.
*'''Third''': Barcelona continued to use their [[2019–20 FC Barcelona season#Kit|2019–20]] [[Senyera]] fourth kit for the third season in a row. This time, it was featured on a more regular basis compared to the previous seasons, and in fact served as a third kit due to the absence of a new third kit with contrasting colors and also without sleeve sponsor.

==Season overview==
===May===
On 31 May, Barcelona announced the signing of [[Sergio Agüero]] from [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]].<ref name="Agüero">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2163393/fc-barcelona-sign-sergio-kun-aguero|title=FC Barcelona sign Sergio 'Kun' Agüero|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=31 May 2021|archive-date=8 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211108011224/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2163393/fc-barcelona-sign-sergio-kun-aguero|url-status=live}}</ref>

===June===
On 1 June, Barcelona announced the signing of [[Eric García (footballer, born 2001)|Eric García]] from Manchester City on a free transfer.<ref name="García">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2163526/eric-garcia-is-fc-barcelonas-second-signing|title=Eric Garcia is FC Barcelona's second signing|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=1 June 2021|archive-date=10 October 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251010141536/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2163526/eric-garcia-is-fc-barcelonas-second-signing|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 2 June, Barcelona announced the signing of [[Emerson Royal]] from [[Real Betis]]. Barça had informed Betis that they would exercise their option to bring back Emerson after his two-year long loan spell with the ''Verdiblancos''.<ref name=Emerson>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2163331/fc-barcelona-sign-emerson|title=FC Barcelona sign Emerson|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=2 June 2021|archive-date=3 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210603082631/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2163331/fc-barcelona-sign-emerson|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 19 June, Barcelona announced the signing of [[Memphis Depay]] from [[Olympique Lyonnais]] on a free transfer.<ref name=Depay>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2174668/memphis-depay-barcas-fourth-signing|title=Memphis Depay, Barça's fourth signing|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=19 June 2021|archive-date=10 October 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251010141530/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2174668/memphis-depay-barcas-fourth-signing|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 27 June, [[OGC Nice]] activated their option to buy [[Jean-Clair Todibo]] permanently from his loan spell for €8.5 million plus €7 million in variables.<ref name=Todibo>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2174555/ogc-nice-exercises-right-to-purchase-jean-clair-todibo|title=OGC Nice exercises right to purchase Jean-Clair Todibo|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=27 June 2021|archive-date=25 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250225081400/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2174555/ogc-nice-exercises-right-to-purchase-jean-clair-todibo|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 29 June, Barcelona and [[Olympique de Marseille]] reached an agreement for the transfer of [[Konrad de la Fuente]] for €3 million. Barça will also receive a percentage of any future transfer fee.<ref name=Konrad>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/barca-b/news/2180134/agreement-for-konrad-de-la-fuente-to-join-olympique-de-marseille|title=Agreement for Konrad de la Fuente to join Olympique de Marseille|date=29 June 2021|publisher=[[FC Barcelona]]|access-date=29 June 2021|archive-date=25 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250225081506/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/barca-b/news/2180134/agreement-for-konrad-de-la-fuente-to-join-olympique-de-marseille|url-status=live}}</ref> Barça also terminated the contract of [[Matheus Fernandes]].<ref name=Matheus>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2180661/matheus-fernandes-contract-terminated|title=Matheus Fernandes' contract terminated|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=29 June 2021|archive-date=29 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210629162135/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2180661/matheus-fernandes-contract-terminated|url-status=live}}</ref>

===July===
On 1 July, [[Lionel Messi]]'s contract expired amidst negotiations to sign a new contract, effectively making Messi a free agent.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Messi officially becomes a free agent as superstar's Barcelona contract expires|url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/messi-free-agent-barcelona-contract-expires/6oic4yrrw62d1mcffybvao1qi|work=Goal|first=Rubén|last=Uría|date=1 July 2021|access-date=1 July 2021|archive-date=27 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211127151900/https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/messi-free-agent-barcelona-contract-expires/6oic4yrrw62d1mcffybvao1qi|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 4 July, Barcelona and [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] reached an agreement for the loan of [[Francisco Trincão]] for the rest of the season with an option to buy for €29 million.<ref name="Trincão">{{cite news|title=Trincão loaned to Wolverhampton Wanderers|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2183128/trincao-loaned-to-wolverhampton-wanderers|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=4 July 2021|access-date=4 July 2021|archive-date=27 October 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251027161254/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2183128/trincao-loaned-to-wolverhampton-wanderers|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 6 July, Barcelona and [[Leeds United F.C|Leeds United]] reached an agreement for the transfer of [[Junior Firpo]] for a fee of €15 million.<ref name=Firpo>{{cite web|title=Agreement with Leeds United for the transfer of Junior Firpo|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2182187/agreement-with-leeds-united-for-the-transfer-of-junior-firpo|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=6 July 2021|archive-date=25 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250225081502/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2182187/agreement-with-leeds-united-for-the-transfer-of-junior-firpo|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 7 July, [[UD Almería]] triggered [[Sergio Akieme]]'s buy option for €3.5 million, with Barcelona reserving a right to 10% of any future sale and a right to first refusal.<ref name=Akieme>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/barca-b/news/2185445/ud-almeria-exercises-option-to-purchase-sergio-akieme-for-35-million-euros|title=UD Almería exercises option to purchase Sergio Akieme for 3.5 million euros|date=7 July 2021|publisher=[[FC Barcelona]]|access-date=8 July 2021|archive-date=7 August 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250807123338/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/barca-b/news/2185445/ud-almeria-exercises-option-to-purchase-sergio-akieme-for-35-million-euros|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 9 July, Barcelona and [[SK Rapid Wien]] reached an agreement over the [[Loan (sports)|loan]] of [[Yusuf Demir]], with Barça receiving an option to buy for €10 million.<ref name=Demir>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/barca-b/news/2186354/agreement-with-sk-rapid-vienna-for-loan-of-yusuf-demir|title=Agreement with SK Rapid Vienna for loan of Yusuf Demir|date=9 July 2021|publisher=[[FC Barcelona]]|access-date=9 July 2021|archive-date=21 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250621164653/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/barca-b/news/2186354/agreement-with-sk-rapid-vienna-for-loan-of-yusuf-demir|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 10 July, Barcelona and [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] reached an agreement for the transfer of [[Carles Aleñá]].<ref name=Alena>{{cite web|title=Agreement with Getafe for the transfer of Carles Aleñá|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2187027/agreement-with-getafe-for-the-transfer-of-carles-alena|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=10 July 2021|archive-date=4 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241204051333/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2187027/agreement-with-getafe-for-the-transfer-of-carles-alena|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 17 July, [[Monchu]] joined [[Granada CF]] on a free deal following the expiration of his contract, with Barça reserving a right to 50% of any future sale, and a right to first refusal with a buyback option.<ref name=Monchu>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/barca-b/news/2190853/monchu-moves-to-granada|title=Monchu moves to Granada|date=16 July 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=17 July 2021|archive-date=25 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250225081318/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/barca-b/news/2190853/monchu-moves-to-granada|url-status=live}}</ref>

===August===
Despite reaching an agreement with Messi and having planned to sign a contract on 5 August, the club announced that Messi would not stay at the club due to financial and structural obstacles posed by [[La Liga]] regulations.<ref name=Messi>{{cite web|title=Leo Messi not staying at FC Barcelona|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2207655/leo-messi-not-staying-at-fc-barcelonaa|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=5 August 2021|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211120157/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2207655/leo-messi-not-staying-at-fc-barcelonaa|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=McVitie|first=Peter|date=5 August 2021|title=Barcelona confirm Messi departure after contract talks break down|url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/barcelona-confirm-messi-departure-after-contract-talks-break/vrjo7e8y4f8k1m50a50dvtg11|archive-url=https://archive.today/20210805181316/https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/barcelona-confirm-messi-departure-after-contract-talks-break/vrjo7e8y4f8k1m50a50dvtg11|archive-date=5 August 2021|work=Goal}}</ref> He subsequently joined [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] on 10 August.<ref name=Messi30>{{cite web|title=Leo Messi signs for Paris Saint-Germain|url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/cp-lionel-messi-psg-paris-saint-germain-mercato|publisher=Paris Saint-Germain|access-date=10 August 2021|archive-date=18 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220718074124/https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/cp-lionel-messi-psg-paris-saint-germain-mercato|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 15 August, Barcelona defeated [[Real Sociedad]] 4–2 at home. Goals from [[Gerard Piqué]], [[Sergi Roberto]] and a brace from [[Martin Braithwaite]] ensured victory in their first [[2021–22 La Liga|La Liga]] match of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2220661/fc-barcelona-4-2-real-sociedad-camp-nou-celebrates-a-winning-start|title=FC Barcelona 4-2 Real Sociedad: Camp Nou celebrates a winning start|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=15 August 2021|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211055300/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2220661/fc-barcelona-4-2-real-sociedad-camp-nou-celebrates-a-winning-start|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 21 August, Barcelona drew with [[Athletic Bilbao]] away at [[San Mamés Stadium (2013)|San Mamés]] in the second match of the season. [[Iñigo Martínez]] scored for Athletic Club, and [[Memphis Depay]] scored his first official goal for Barça to end the match 1–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2227561/athletic-club-1-1-barca-all-square-at-san-mames|title=Athletic Club 1-1 Barça: All square at San Mamés|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=22 August 2021|archive-date=27 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127003650/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2227561/athletic-club-1-1-barca-all-square-at-san-mames|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 29 August, Barcelona defeated [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] 2–1 at home, thanks to goals from Sergi Roberto and Memphis Depay.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2238832/barca-2-1-getafe-another-victory-at-camp-nou|title=Barça 2-1 Getafe: Another victory at Camp Nou|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=29 August 2021|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211070553/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2238832/barca-2-1-getafe-another-victory-at-camp-nou|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 31 August, Barcelona reached an agreement with [[RB Leipzig]] for the transfer of [[Ilaix Moriba]] for €16 million with €6 million in add-ons;<ref name=Ilaix>{{cite web|title=Agreement with RB Leipzig for the transfer of Ilaix Moriba|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/barca-b/news/2239557/agreement-with-rb-leipzig-for-the-transfer-of-ilaix-moriba|access-date=2021-08-31|website=www.fcbarcelona.com|language=en|archive-date=25 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250225081359/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/barca-b/news/2239557/agreement-with-rb-leipzig-for-the-transfer-of-ilaix-moriba|url-status=live}}</ref> reached an agreement with [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] for the transfer of [[Emerson Royal]] for €25 million;<ref name=Royal>{{cite web|title=Agreement with Tottenham Hotspur for the transfer of Emerson Royal|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2240292/agreement-with-tottenham-hotspur-for-the-transfer-of-emerson-royal|access-date=2021-08-31|website=www.fcbarcelona.com|language=en|archive-date=25 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250425083059/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2240292/agreement-with-tottenham-hotspur-for-the-transfer-of-emerson-royal|url-status=live}}</ref> and reached an agreement with [[Atlético Madrid]] for the loan of [[Antoine Griezmann]] for a reported fee of €10 million with a mandatory buy option of €40 million.<ref name=Griezmann>{{cite web|title=Agreement with Atlético Madrid for the loan of Antoine Griezmann|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2240697/agreement-with-atletico-madrid-for-the-loan-of-antoine-griezmann|access-date=1 September 2021|website=www.fcbarcelona.com|language=en|archive-date=1 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210901045020/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2240697/agreement-with-atletico-madrid-for-the-loan-of-antoine-griezmann|url-status=live}}</ref> Barça also announced the signing of [[Luuk de Jong]] from [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] on a season long loan with an option to buy.<ref name=Luuk>{{cite web|title=Agreement with Sevilla for the loan of Luuk de Jong|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2240705/agreement-with-sevilla-for-the-loan-of-luuk-de-jong|access-date=1 September 2021|website=www.fcbarcelona.com|language=en|archive-date=1 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210901092228/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2240705/agreement-with-sevilla-for-the-loan-of-luuk-de-jong|url-status=live}}</ref>

===September===
On 2 September, Barcelona and [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] reached an agreement for the loan of [[Miralem Pjanić]] for the rest of the season.<ref name=Pjanic>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2242603/agreement-with-besiktas-for-the-loan-of-miralem-pjanic|title=Agreement with Besiktas for the loan of Miralem Pjanic|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=5 September 2021|archive-date=24 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250324063342/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2242603/agreement-with-besiktas-for-the-loan-of-miralem-pjanic|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 14 September, Barcelona lost 3–0 at home to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in the first [[UEFA Champions League]] game of the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|season]]. [[Thomas Müller]] and [[Robert Lewandowski]] (brace) scored for the ''Bavarians''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2255294/fc-barcelona-0-3-bayern-munich-disappointing-start-to-champions-league-campaign |title=FC Barcelona 0-3 Bayern Munich: Disappointing start to Champions League campaign |date=14 September 2021 |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=17 September 2021 |archive-date=13 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250213194914/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2255294/fc-barcelona-0-3-bayern-munich-disappointing-start-to-champions-league-campaign |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 20 September, Barcelona drew 1–1 with [[Granada CF|Granada]] at home. Barça conceded early in the match, but a goal from [[Ronald Araújo]] in the last minute of the game levelled the score.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2263923/barca-1-1-granada-incomplete-fightback|title=Barça 1-1 Granada: Incomplete fightback|date=20 September 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 September 2021|archive-date=4 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241204163535/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2263923/barca-1-1-granada-incomplete-fightback|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 23 September, Barcelona drew 0–0 with [[Cádiz CF|Cádiz]] away from home.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2266522/fc-barcelona-0-0-cadiz-no-goals|title=FC Barcelona 0-0 Cádiz: No goals|date=23 September 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=24 September 2021|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211070741/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2266522/fc-barcelona-0-0-cadiz-no-goals|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 26 September, Barcelona defeated [[Levante UD|Levante]] 3–0 at home. Memphis, [[Luuk de Jong]] and [[Ansu Fati]] were the goalscorers, with the latter making his return after a 10-month absence due to injury. De Jong also scored his first goal for Barça.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2271612/barca-3-0-levante-party-time-at-camp-nou|title=Barça 3-0 Levante: Party time at Camp Nou!|date=26 September 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=26 September 2021|archive-date=20 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250420200541/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2271612/barca-3-0-levante-party-time-at-camp-nou|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 29 September, Barcelona lost 3–0 against [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] away from home on the second matchday of the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2274806/benfica-3-0-fc-barcelona-painful-defeat-in-lisbon|title=Benfica 3-0 FC Barcelona: Painful defeat in Lisbon|date=29 September 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=29 September 2021|archive-date=22 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250522100507/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2274806/benfica-3-0-fc-barcelona-painful-defeat-in-lisbon|url-status=live}}</ref>

===October===
On 2 October, Barcelona lost 2–0 against [[Atlético Madrid]] away from home. [[Thomas Lemar]] and former Barça player [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] scored the goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2279471/atletico-madrid-2-0-fc-barcelona-first-liga-defeat|title=Atlético Madrid 2-0 FC Barcelona: First Liga defeat|date=2 October 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=2 October 2021|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211055043/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2279471/atletico-madrid-2-0-fc-barcelona-first-liga-defeat|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 14 October, Barcelona and midfielder [[Pedri]] reached an agreement to extend the player's contract for a further four seasons through to 2026 with a release clause of €1 billion.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2288606/pedri-contract-extension-to-2026 |title=Pedri contract extension to 2026 |date=14 October 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=21 May 2022 |archive-date=14 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250714115928/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2288606/pedri-contract-extension-to-2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 17 October, Barcelona defeated [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] 3–1 at home. Valencia took the lead early in the match, but goals from Fati, Memphis and [[Philippe Coutinho]] ensured victory for Barça.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2295131/fc-barcelona-3-1-valencia-back-on-track|title=FC Barcelona 3-1 Valencia: Back on track|date=17 October 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=18 October 2021|archive-date=23 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250423175402/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2295131/fc-barcelona-3-1-valencia-back-on-track|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 20 October, Barcelona defeated [[FC Dynamo Kyiv|Dynamo Kyiv]] 1–0 at home in the Champions league. Piqué scored the only goal in the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2299660/fc-barcelona-1-0-dynamo-kyiv-off-the-mark|title=FC Barcelona 1-0 Dynamo Kyiv: Off the mark|date=20 October 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=20 October 2021|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211140925/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2299660/fc-barcelona-1-0-dynamo-kyiv-off-the-mark|url-status=live}}</ref> Later that day Barcelona announced that they had reached an agreement with [[Ansu Fati]] to extend the player's contract for a further five seasons through to 2027 with a release clause of €1 billion.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2298544/ansu-fati-culer-until-2027 |title=Ansu Fati, culer until 2027 |date=20 October 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=21 May 2022 |archive-date=15 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250615092823/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2298544/ansu-fati-culer-until-2027 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 24 October, Barcelona were defeated in [[El Clásico]] 2–1 at home, with [[David Alaba]] and [[Lucas Vázquez]] scoring for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]. Sergio Agüero scored in the last minute for a late consolation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/matches/68543/fc-barcelona-r-madrid-la-liga-2021-2022|title=FC Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid: Defeat in a tight clásico|date=24 October 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=24 October 2021|archive-date=18 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240718135831/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/matches/68543/fc-barcelona-r-madrid-la-liga-2021-2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 27 October, Barcelona were again defeated, this time by [[Rayo Vallecano]] 1–0 away, with [[Radamel Falcao]] scoring the winner in the first half.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/matches/68557/rayo-fc-barcelona-la-liga-2021-2022|title=Rayo Vallecano 1-0 FC Barcelona: Cruel defeat at Vallecas|date=27 October 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=27 October 2021|archive-date=13 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250213162120/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/matches/68557/rayo-fc-barcelona-la-liga-2021-2022|url-status=live}}</ref> It was Rayo's first league win over Barça in 19 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-spain-ray-fcb-report/soccer-rayo-vallecano-hand-sloppy-barcelona-defeat-koeman-sacked-idUKKBN2HH2KT|title=Rayo Vallecano hand sloppy Barcelona defeat, Koeman sacked|date=27 October 2021|publisher=[[Reuters]]|access-date=30 October 2021|archive-date=23 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123145651/https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-spain-ray-fcb-report/soccer-rayo-vallecano-hand-sloppy-barcelona-defeat-koeman-sacked-idUKKBN2HH2KT/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 28 October, Barcelona announced the dismissal of [[Ronald Koeman]] as the first team coach, ending his spell at the club after 14 months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2311932/ronald-koeman-relieved-of-his-duties-as-first-team-coach|title=Ronald Koeman relieved of his duties as first team coach|date=28 October 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=28 October 2021|archive-date=1 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201081730/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2311932/ronald-koeman-relieved-of-his-duties-as-first-team-coach|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 29 October, Barcelona announced the appointment of [[Barcelona B]] head coach [[Sergi Barjuán]] as the [[Interim management|interim manager]] of the first team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2312224/sergi-barjuan-caretaker-coach-of-fc-barcelona|title=Sergi Barjuan, caretaker coach of FC Barcelona|date=29 October 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=29 October 2021|archive-date=7 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241107073831/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2312224/sergi-barjuan-caretaker-coach-of-fc-barcelona|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 30 October, Barcelona drew 1–1 with [[Deportivo Alavés]] at home. Memphis scored first for the ''Blaugrana'', but Alavés equalised shortly after, courtesy of [[Luis Rioja]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2317826/barca-1-1-alaves-held-to-a-draw|title=Barça 1-1 Alavés: Held to a draw|date=30 October 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=3 November 2021|archive-date=22 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250522110238/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2317826/barca-1-1-alaves-held-to-a-draw|url-status=live}}</ref>

===November===
On 2 November, Barcelona defeated Dynamo Kyiv 1–0 away from home in the Champions league. Ansu Fati scored the only goal in the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2327590/dynamo-kyiv-0-1-fc-barcelona-job-done|title=Dynamo Kyiv 0-1 FC Barcelona: Job done!|date=2 November 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=3 November 2021|archive-date=27 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250427231336/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2327590/dynamo-kyiv-0-1-fc-barcelona-job-done|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 6 November, Barcelona announced the appointment of [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]] as the new first team head coach until 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2328587/xavi-hernandez-is-the-new-fc-barcelona-coach|title=Xavi Hernández is the new FC Barcelona coach|date=6 November 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=6 November 2021|archive-date=6 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211106005657/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2328587/xavi-hernandez-is-the-new-fc-barcelona-coach|url-status=live}}</ref> Later that day, Barcelona drew 3–3 with [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] away from home. Barça had a three-goal lead within the first half with goals from Fati, [[Sergio Busquets|Busquets]] and Memphis, but a spirited performance from Celta levelled the score in the second half with the equalising goal from [[Iago Aspas]] coming in the final minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2341438/celta-3-3-barca-a-game-of-two-halves|title=Celta 3-3 Barça: A game of two halves|date=6 November 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=7 November 2021|archive-date=19 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250319032349/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2341438/celta-3-3-barca-a-game-of-two-halves|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 12 November, Barcelona announced an agreement in principle to sign former right-back [[Dani Alves]] on a free transfer.<ref name=Alves>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2349770/agreement-in-principle-to-sign-dani-alves|title=Agreement in principle to sign Dani Alves|date=12 November 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=12 November 2021|archive-date=26 August 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250826091959/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2349770/agreement-in-principle-to-sign-dani-alves|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 20 November, on Xavi's managerial debut, Barcelona defeated [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] 1–0 at home in the [[derbi barceloní]]. Memphis scored from the penalty spot.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2361670/barca-1-0-espanyol-winning-start-for-xavi|title=Barça 1-0 Espanyol: Winning start for Xavi|date=20 November 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=26 November 2021|archive-date=14 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250514203734/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2361670/barca-1-0-espanyol-winning-start-for-xavi|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 23 November, Barcelona drew 0–0 with Benfica at home in the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2366776/barca-0-0-benfica-all-to-be-decided-in-munich|title=Barça 0-0 Benfica: All to be decided in Munich|date=23 November 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=24 November 2021|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211055630/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2366776/barca-0-0-benfica-all-to-be-decided-in-munich|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 27 November, Barcelona defeated [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] 3–1 away from home. [[Frenkie de Jong]] scored first, but [[Samuel Chukwueze]] equalised for the ''Yellow Submarine''. Memphis and Coutinho scored late to seal the win for Barça.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2374350/villarreal-1-3-fc-barcelona-away-win-with-character|title=Villarreal 1-3 FC Barcelona: Away win with character|date=27 November 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=29 November 2021|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211162632/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2374350/villarreal-1-3-fc-barcelona-away-win-with-character|url-status=live}}</ref>

===December===
On 4 December, Barcelona lost to Real Betis 1–0 at home. [[Juanmi (footballer, born 1993)|Juanmi]] scored for the visitors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2394352/barca-01-betis-first-defeat-of-the-xavi-era|title=Barça 0–1 Betis: First defeat of the Xavi era|date=4 December 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=5 November 2021|archive-date=21 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250321095016/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2394352/barca-01-betis-first-defeat-of-the-xavi-era|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 8 December, Barcelona lost to Bayern 3–0 away from home at an empty [[Allianz Arena]]. Müller, [[Leroy Sané]] and [[Jamal Musiala]] scored for the home side, eliminating Barça from the group stage and making the ''Blaugrana'' play in the [[UEFA Europa League]] for the first time since [[2003–04 FC Barcelona season|2003]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2407087/bayern-munich-3-0-fc-barcelona-out-of-the-champions-league|title=Bayern Munich 3-0 FC Barcelona: Out of the Champions League|date=8 December 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=9 December 2021|archive-date=21 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250121091616/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2407087/bayern-munich-3-0-fc-barcelona-out-of-the-champions-league|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2407065/fc-barcelona-fail-to-extend-17-year-streak-in-champions-league-last-sixteen|title=FC Barcelona fail to extend 17-year streak in Champions League last sixteen|date=8 December 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=9 November 2021|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211065409/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2407065/fc-barcelona-fail-to-extend-17-year-streak-in-champions-league-last-sixteen|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 9 December, Barcelona and Granada reached an agreement for the loan of [[Álex Collado]] until the end of the season.<ref name="Collado">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2408159/alex-collado-loaned-to-granada|title=Àlex Collado loaned to Granada|date=9 December 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=9 November 2021|archive-date=3 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241203160302/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2408159/alex-collado-loaned-to-granada|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 12 December, Barcelona drew 2–2 with [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] away from home. [[Nico González (footballer, born 2002)|Nico]] and [[Abde Ezzalzouli|Abde]] scored for Barca.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2413281/osasuna-2-2-barca-late-equaliser-denies-victory-at-el-sadar|title=Osasuna 2-2 Barça: Late equaliser denies victory at El Sadar|date=12 December 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=26 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126225013/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2413281/osasuna-2-2-barca-late-equaliser-denies-victory-at-el-sadar|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 15 December, Sergio Agüero announced his retirement in a press conference at the [[Camp Nou]].<ref name="AgüeroRET">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2416373/sergio-kun-aguero-retires-a-legendary-goalscorer|title=Sergio "Kun" Agüero retires, a legendary goalscorer|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=15 December 2021|archive-date=29 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211229203923/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2416373/sergio-kun-aguero-retires-a-legendary-goalscorer/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 18 December, Barcelona defeated [[Elche CF|Elche]] 3–2 at home. Goals from [[Ferran Jutglà]] and [[Gavi (footballer)|Gavi]] gave an early two goal lead for Barça, But two goals scored by Elche in two minutes made the score level. Nico scored in the late stages of the game to earn victory for Barça.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2421331/barca-3-2-elche-victory-for-the-future|title=Barça 3-2 Elche: Victory for the future|date=18 December 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=9 April 2022|archive-date=13 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250113235724/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2421331/barca-3-2-elche-victory-for-the-future|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 21 December, Barcelona drew 1–1 with [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] at the [[Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium|Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán]], with [[Papu Gómez]] opening the account for ''Los Rojiblancos'' and Araújo equalising in the dying moments of the first–half.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2425321/sevilla-1-1-fc-barcelona-promising-point-to-end-the-year|title=Sevilla 1-1 FC Barcelona: Promising point to end the year|date=21 December 2021|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=23 December 2021|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211140541/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2425321/sevilla-1-1-fc-barcelona-promising-point-to-end-the-year|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 28 December, Barcelona announced the signing of [[Ferran Torres]], with Torres signing a 5-year contract until 2027, with a buyout clause of €1 billion.<ref name="Torres">{{Cite web|title=FC Barcelona signs Ferran Torres|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2426442/fc-barcelona-signs-ferran-torres|access-date=2021-12-28|website=www.fcbarcelona.com|language=en|archive-date=19 August 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250819071325/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2426442/fc-barcelona-signs-ferran-torres|url-status=live}}</ref>

===January===
On 2 January, Barcelona defeated [[RCD Mallorca|Real Mallorca]] 1–0 at the [[Visit Mallorca Stadium]]. Luuk de Jong scored the only goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2438370/mallorca-0-1-fc-barcelona-happy-new-year|title=Mallorca 0-1 FC Barcelona: Happy new year!|date=2 January 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=2 January 2022|archive-date=29 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929051524/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2438370/mallorca-0-1-fc-barcelona-happy-new-year|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 5 January, Barcelona started their [[2021-22 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] campaign with a 2–1 away win against [[Linares Deportivo|Linares]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2440787/linares-deportivo-1-2-fc-barcelona-late-recovery-to-reach-last-16|title=Linares Deportivo 1-2 FC Barcelona: Late recovery to reach last 16|date=5 January 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=5 January 2022|archive-date=23 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250423174518/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2440787/linares-deportivo-1-2-fc-barcelona-late-recovery-to-reach-last-16|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 7 January, Barcelona reached an agreement with [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] for the loan of Philippe Coutinho until the end of the season.<ref name="Coutinho">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2441508/philippe-coutinho-loaned-out-to-aston-villa-until-the-end-of-the-season|title=Philippe Coutinho loaned out to Aston Villa until the end of the season|date=7 January 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=7 January 2022|archive-date=2 October 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251002000114/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2441508/philippe-coutinho-loaned-out-to-aston-villa-until-the-end-of-the-season|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 8 January, Barcelona drew 1–1 with [[Granada CF|Granada]] away from home. Luuk de Jong took the lead for Barcelona but Granada equalised at the closing stages of the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2442966/granada-1-1-barca-denied-at-the-death|title=Granada 1-1 Barça: Denied at the death|date=8 January 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=26 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126225006/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2442966/granada-1-1-barca-denied-at-the-death|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 10 January, [[Samuel Umtiti]] extended his contract until 2026, which allowed Barcelona to register Ferran Torres.<ref name="Umtiti extension">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2441748/samuel-umtiti-contract-extended-to-2026-with-reduction-of-part-of-his-salary|title=Samuel Umtiti contract extended to 2026 with reduction of part of his salary|date=10 January 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=10 January 2022|archive-date=19 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250319030238/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2441748/samuel-umtiti-contract-extended-to-2026-with-reduction-of-part-of-his-salary|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 12 January, the second Clásico of the season was contested, this time at the semi-final stage of the [[2021–22 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]]. Luuk de Jong and Ansu Fati scored equalisers for Barça, but it was not enough as Madrid won 3–2 after extra time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2022/01/13/football/real-madrid-barcelona-supercup-el-clasico-spt-intl/index.html|title=Real Madrid beats Barcelona for 100th El Clasico victory to reach Spanish Supercup final|date=12 January 2022|publisher=[[CNN]]|access-date=15 January 2022|archive-date=24 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124190408/https://edition.cnn.com/2022/01/13/football/real-madrid-barcelona-supercup-el-clasico-spt-intl/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 13 January, Barcelona reached an agreement with [[SK Rapid Wien|Rapid Wien]] to end the loan of [[Yusuf Demir]].<ref name="Demir loan return">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2446290/agreement-to-terminate-yusuf-demir-loan|title=Agreement to terminate Yusuf Demir loan|date=13 January 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=13 January 2022|archive-date=11 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250211152320/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2446290/agreement-to-terminate-yusuf-demir-loan|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 20 January, Barcelona were knocked out of the Copa del Rey round of 16 by Athletic Bilbao 3–2 at San Mamés, with [[Iker Muniain]]'s late winner cancelling out Ferran Torres and [[Pedri]]'s goals, with the former scoring his first Barça goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2456430/athletic-club-3-2-barca-copa-del-rey-defence-ends-in-extra-time|title=Athletic Club 3-2 Barça: Copa del Rey defence ends in extra time|date=20 January 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=29 January 2022|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211055107/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2456430/athletic-club-3-2-barca-copa-del-rey-defence-ends-in-extra-time|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 23 January, Barcelona defeated Deportivo Alavés 1–0 away, thanks to a late winner from Frenkie de Jong.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2462214/alaves-0-1-fc-barcelona-late-winner-secures-vital-victory|title=Alavés 0-1 FC Barcelona: Late winner secures vital victory|date=23 January 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=29 January 2022|archive-date=12 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241212021322/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2462214/alaves-0-1-fc-barcelona-late-winner-secures-vital-victory|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 29 January, Barcelona announced the signing of [[Adama Traoré (footballer, born 1996)|Adama Traoré]] on loan from [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]].<ref name="Traoré">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2465304/adama-traore-comes-to-fc-barcelona-on-loan|title=Adama Traoré comes to FC Barcelona on loan|date=29 January 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=29 January 2022|archive-date=27 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250427233726/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2465304/adama-traore-comes-to-fc-barcelona-on-loan|url-status=live}}</ref>

===February===
On 5 February, Barcelona announced the signing of [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]] for free after his contract with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] was terminated.<ref name="Aubameyang">{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2467985/fc-barcelona-sign-pierre-emerick-aubameyang|title=FC Barcelona sign Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang|date=2 February 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=2 February 2022|archive-date=22 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220222095446/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2467985/fc-barcelona-sign-pierre-emerick-aubameyang|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 6 February, Barcelona defeated Atletico Madrid 4–2 at home. Atletico took an early lead but goals from [[Jordi Alba]], Gavi, Araújo and [[Dani Alves]] provided a convincing victory for Barça.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2473806/fc-barcelona-4-2-atletico-madrid-glorious-return-to-camp-nou|title=FC Barcelona 4-2 Atlético Madrid: Glorious return to Camp Nou|date=6 February 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=11 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250211151105/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2473806/fc-barcelona-4-2-atletico-madrid-glorious-return-to-camp-nou|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 13 February, Barcelona drew 2–2 with Espanyol away from home. Pedri scored an early goal to give lead for Barça, but two goals from the home side almost made them win the match before a late goal from Luuk de Jong which earned a point for Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2485785/rcd-espanyol-2-2-fc-barcelona-luuk-de-jong-to-the-late-rescue|title=RCD Espanyol 2-2 FC Barcelona: Luuk de Jong to the late rescue!|date=13 February 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=29 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250429065928/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2485785/rcd-espanyol-2-2-fc-barcelona-luuk-de-jong-to-the-late-rescue|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 17 February, Barcelona opened their Europa league campaign with a 1–1 draw with [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] at home in the first leg of the round of 32. Napoli scored first and Ferran Torres converted a penalty to level the score.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2489858/fc-barcelona-1-1-napoli-all-to-play-for-in-naples|title=FC Barcelona 1-1 Napoli: All to play for in Naples|date=17 February 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211055141/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2489858/fc-barcelona-1-1-napoli-all-to-play-for-in-naples|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 20 February, Barcelona defeated Valencia 4–1 away from home. A goal from Frenkie de Jong  and a hat-trick from Aubameyang gained victory over Los Che.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2495932/valencia-1-4-fc-barcelona-rampant-at-mestalla|title=Valencia 1-4 FC Barcelona: Rampant at Mestalla|date=20 February 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211060649/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2495932/valencia-1-4-fc-barcelona-rampant-at-mestalla|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 24 February, Barcelona defeated Napoli 4–2 away from home in the second leg of the Europa League round of 32. Jordi Alba, Frenkie de Jong, Pique and Aubameyang scored for Barça.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2503257/napoli-2-4-fc-barcelona-bellissimo|title=Napoli 2-4 FC Barcelona: Bellissimo!|date=24 February 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=11 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211054746/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2503257/napoli-2-4-fc-barcelona-bellissimo|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 27 February, Barcelona defeated Athletic Bilbao 4–0 at home. Aubameyang, Dembélé, Luuk de Jong and Memphis Depay scored for Barcelona to secure three points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2508360/fc-barcelona-4-0-athletic-club-four-goals-again|title=FC Barcelona 4-0 Athletic Club: Four goals again!|date=27 February 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=5 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241205112355/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2508360/fc-barcelona-4-0-athletic-club-four-goals-again|url-status=live}}</ref>

===March===
On 6 March, Barcelona defeated Elche 2–1 away from home. Elche scored late in the first half, but goals from Torres and Depay turned the game in favour of Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2518664/elche-1-2-fc-barcelona-second-half-comeback|title=Elche 1-2 FC Barcelona: Second half comeback|date=6 March 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=21 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250621233733/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2518664/elche-1-2-fc-barcelona-second-half-comeback|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 10 March, Barcelona drew 0–0 with [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] at home in the first leg of the Europa League round of 16.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2524525/barca-0-0-galatasaray-to-be-decided-in-istanbul|title=Barça 0-0 Galatasaray: To be decided in Istanbul|date=10 March 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=30 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231130114222/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2524525/barca-0-0-galatasaray-to-be-decided-in-istanbul|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 13 March, Barcelona defeated Osasuna 4–0 at home. Ferran Torres scored a brace while Aubameyang and [[Riqui Puig]] added a goal each.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2532288/barca-4-0-osasuna-perfect-night-at-camp-nou|title=Barça 4-0 Osasuna: Perfect night at Camp Nou|date=13 March 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=23 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123181322/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2532288/barca-4-0-osasuna-perfect-night-at-camp-nou|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 17 March, Barcelona defeated Galatasaray 2–1 away from home in the second leg of the Europa League round of 16. Galatasaray scored the first goal of the match but goals from Pedri and Aubameyang cancelled out their lead and secured 2–1 aggregate victory for Barça.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2539150/galatasaray-1-2-fc-barcelona-comeback-in-istanbul|title=Galatasaray 1-2 FC Barcelona: Comeback in Istanbul|date=17 March 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=7 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241207084415/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2539150/galatasaray-1-2-fc-barcelona-comeback-in-istanbul|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 20 March, in the third Clásico of the season, Barcelona defeated Real Madrid 4–0 away from home. A brace from Aubameyang and goals from Araújo and Torres secured a crushing victory at the Bernabeu.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2544426/real-madrid-0-4-barca-the-clasico-is-blaugrana|title=Real Madrid 0-4 Barça: The Clásico is blaugrana!|date=20 March 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=2 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241202172233/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2544426/real-madrid-0-4-barca-the-clasico-is-blaugrana|url-status=live}}</ref>

===April===
On 3 April, Barcelona defeated Sevilla 1–0 at home. Pedri scored the only goal of the match. With this win, Barça climes up to second in the league standings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2562062/fc-barcelona-1-0-sevilla-up-to-second|title=FC Barcelona 1-0 Sevilla: Up to second!|date=20 March 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=21 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250321113226/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2562062/fc-barcelona-1-0-sevilla-up-to-second|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 7 April, Barcelona drew 1–1 with [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] away from home in the first leg of the Europa League quarter-finals. Ferran Torres scored for Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2566760/eintracht-11-barca-all-square-in-frankfurt|title=Eintracht 1–1 Barça: All square in Frankfurt|date=7 March 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=21 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250421201928/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2566760/eintracht-11-barca-all-square-in-frankfurt|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 10 April, Barcelona defeated Levante 3–2 away from home. Aubameyang and Pedri scored for Barça while having conceded two penalties. Luuk de Jong scored a late goal to earn the victory for Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2572391/levante-2-3-fc-barcelona-dramatic-win-at-the-ciutat-de-valencia|title=Levante 2-3 FC Barcelona: Dramatic win at the Ciutat de València|date=10 April 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=22 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240622070558/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2572391/levante-2-3-fc-barcelona-dramatic-win-at-the-ciutat-de-valencia|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 14 April, Barcelona lost to Eintracht Frankfurt 3–2 at home in the second leg of the Europa League quarter-finals. Frankfurt dominated the game having a three-goal lead until the end of the regulation time. Barcelona's goals came in the stoppage time with Busquets scoring and Depay converting a penalty. With an aggregate score of 4–3, Barcelona were eliminated from the Europa League.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2575655/fc-barcelona-23-eintracht-frankfurt-out-of-the-europa-league|title=FC Barcelona 2–3 Eintracht Frankfurt: Out of the Europa League|date=14 April 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=23 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240723114501/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2575655/fc-barcelona-23-eintracht-frankfurt-out-of-the-europa-league|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 18 April, Barcelona lost to Cádiz 1–0 at home.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2579803/fc-barcelona-0-1-cadiz-disappointment-at-camp-nou|title=FC Barcelona 0-1 Cádiz: Disappointment at Camp Nou|date=18 April 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=19 July 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250719150824/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2579803/fc-barcelona-0-1-cadiz-disappointment-at-camp-nou|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 21 April, Barcelona defeated Real Sociedad 1–0 away from home. Aubameyang scored the only goal in the first half of the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2585123/real-sociedad-0-1-fc-barcelona-show-of-strength-at-reale-arena|title=Real Sociedad 0-1 FC Barcelona: Show of strength at Reale Arena|date=21 April 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=26 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126224853/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2585123/real-sociedad-0-1-fc-barcelona-show-of-strength-at-reale-arena|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 24 April, Barcelona lost to Rayo Vallecano 1–0 at home.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2591210/barca-0-1-rayo-vallecano-another-upset-at-camp-nou|title=Barça 0-1 Rayo Vallecano: Another upset at Camp Nou|date=24 April 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=26 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126224927/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2591210/barca-0-1-rayo-vallecano-another-upset-at-camp-nou|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 26 April, Barcelona and defender Ronald Araújo reached an agreement to extend the player's contract through to 2026 with a release clause of €1 billion.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2592089/agreement-for-new-contract-for-ronald-araujo |title=Agreement for new contract for Ronald Araujo |date=26 April 2022 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=21 May 2022 |archive-date=15 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250215194042/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2592089/agreement-for-new-contract-for-ronald-araujo |url-status=live}}</ref>

===May===
On 1 May, Barcelona defeated Real Mallorca 2–1 at home. Memphis Depay and Sergio Busquets scored for Barça.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2601197/fc-barcelona-2-1-mallorca-a-much-needed-win|title=FC Barcelona 2-1 Mallorca: A much-needed win|date=1 May 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=23 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123145743/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2601197/fc-barcelona-2-1-mallorca-a-much-needed-win|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 7 May, Barcelona defeated Real Betis 2–1 away from home. Ansu Fati scored while former Barça player [[Marc Bartra]] scored the equaliser for Betis. Jordi Alba scored in the final minutes of the match to earn the victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2608680/real-betis-1-2-fc-barcelona-mission-accomplished|title=Real Betis 1-2 FC Barcelona: Mission accomplished!|date=7 May 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=23 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123151236/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2608680/real-betis-1-2-fc-barcelona-mission-accomplished|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 10 May, Barcelona defeated Celta Vigo 3–1 at home. Memphis scored a goal while Aubameyang added a brace.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2613055/barca-3-1-celta-eventful-win-at-camp-nou|title=Barça 3-1 Celta: Eventful win at Camp Nou|date=10 May 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=26 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126224950/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2613055/barca-3-1-celta-eventful-win-at-camp-nou|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 12 May, Aston Villa triggered Philippe Coutinho's option to buy for a fee of €20 million with Barça receiving a 50% sell-on percentage.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2613776/agreement-with-aston-villa-to-transfer-philippe-coutinho|title=Agreement with Aston Villa to transfer Philippe Coutinho|date=12 May 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=5 August 2022|archive-date=2 October 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251002002325/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2613776/agreement-with-aston-villa-to-transfer-philippe-coutinho|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 15 May, Barcelona drew 0–0 with Getafe away from home.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2619821/getafe-00-fc-barcelona-job-done|title=Getafe 0–0 FC Barcelona: Job done|date=15 May 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=21 May 2022|archive-date=26 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250326021221/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2619821/getafe-00-fc-barcelona-job-done|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 22 May, Barcelona lost to Villarreal 2–0 at home in the last game of the season. Barcelona finished their league campaign in the second position, qualifying for the next season's [[2022–23 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] and [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2632364/fc-barcelona-0-2-villarreal-final-day-defeat|title=FC Barcelona 0-2 Villarreal: Final day defeat|date=22 May 2022|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=28 May 2022|archive-date=23 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123151245/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2632364/fc-barcelona-0-2-villarreal-final-day-defeat|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/61545978|title=Barcelona 0-2 Villarreal: Barca end on lowest La Liga points haul since 2008|date=22 May 2022|publisher=BBC.com|access-date=28 May 2022|archive-date=28 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220528114726/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/61545978|url-status=live}}</ref>
